name: tabularia
description: Read and revise novels, nonfiction, articles, and scripts in Tabularia with ChatGPT: developmental reads, continuity checks, line edits, synopses, and screenplay coverage, with changes in drafts you review and merge as you choose.

interface.longDescription: Tabularia is a writing studio for books, articles, and scripts, designed to help you manage the complexity of large projects with easy outlining, fast navigation, and custom timelines. Connect it to ChatGPT and you have an editor who can read, recommend, and revise any part of your manuscript. Open a published page and ask ChatGPT to read it aloud; it finds the page itself and highlights each sentence as it speaks. ChatGPT proposes changes in drafts that leave your own text untouched until you merge them, or edits your text directly when you ask, saving a snapshot of your work first. It can also add comments, notes, timeline markers, and images; set up your book's title page, chapters, and styles; and add design touches like drop caps and ornaments.
capabilities: Line edits proposed in a draft you review
Book design: title pages, chapter openings, drop caps
Pictures from Wikimedia Commons, Unsplash, and Flickr

defaultPrompt: Help me create or import my first project in Tabularia, then show me where to open and edit it.
Does the middle of my novel drag?
Make character sheets from my manuscript.

positive.description: Lists the manuscripts in the signed-in account without changing anything.
positive.prompt: What manuscripts do I have in Tabularia?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the account's manuscripts by title, among them Dracula, Pride and Prejudice, Alice in Wonderland, and The Count of Monte Cristo. Nothing in the account changes.

positive.description: Answers a question about a manuscript from its own text.
positive.prompt: In Dracula, where does Jonathan Harker first mention the crucifix, and who gave it to him?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the passage in Harker's journal in Chapter 1 where the landlord's wife at the Golden Krone in Bistritz hangs a crucifix around his neck, and quotes it. Nothing in the account changes.

positive.description: Proposes a line edit in a draft and leaves the manuscript itself untouched.
positive.prompt: Line-edit the opening paragraph of Alice in Wonderland in a draft I can review. Don't change my text.
positive.expected_behavior: Puts the edits in the assistant's own draft, summarizes them, and says where to review them in Tabularia. The manuscript's own text is unchanged until the Writer merges.

positive.description: Builds character Sheets from the text.
positive.prompt: Make character sheets for the five Bennet sisters in Pride and Prejudice.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes five character Sheets, one each for Jane, Elizabeth, Mary, Kitty, and Lydia Bennet, each drawn from the text. Asking again updates those Sheets rather than duplicating them.

positive.description: Builds a timeline of a story thread from the text.
positive.prompt: Build a timeline of Edmond Dantès's arrest, imprisonment, and escape in The Count of Monte Cristo.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a Timeline and marks the arrest at the betrothal feast, the imprisonment in the Château d'If, and the escape in Faria's burial sack, then names the Timeline so the Writer can open it in Tabularia.

negative.description: Deleting a manuscript is not something the plugin can do. The assistant says so and points the Writer to Tabularia, without calling a tool that changes the account.
negative.prompt: Delete The Count of Monte Cristo from my Tabularia account.

negative.description: Sending a draft to someone else is the Writer's action, never the assistant's. The assistant explains that it cannot send and that the Writer sends an invitation from the Sharing panel.
negative.prompt: Email my Dracula draft to my editor at editor@example.com.

negative.description: The plugin reaches only the signed-in account. A request for another person's manuscripts is declined without any tool call.
negative.prompt: Open the manuscripts in my friend Maria's Tabularia account.

review.commerce_description: The plugin does not sell anything or take payments. Tabularia subscriptions are bought on tabularia.app, not through ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: ChatGPT can now read your published pages aloud. Open the page and ask; it finds the page itself and highlights each sentence as it speaks, and you can click any word to carry on from there. Three new skills: one finds the right page or manuscript and reads it aloud, one helps you choose or record the story shape your book follows and reads your draft against it, and one lets ChatGPT pick up an interrupted change without making it twice. ChatGPT can also set your book's headers, footers, and margin numbers, and it tells you who made each edit when it reads a passage.
